specialty: pre-seal/full-history/linear Git provenance and wave seals

findings.title: Prebaseline lane history still uses path-simplified Git traversal
findings.claim: The lock creator and post-lock validator can miss a prohibited lane artifact that is introduced and removed on a side branch and then merged into the v2 baseline. The reachable baseline history contains the artifact, but historical_lane_files returns an empty set because it omits --full-history; merge rejection begins after the baseline and therefore does not reject a merge that is itself the baseline.
findings.evidence: scripts/create_correctness_audit_lock.py:101-116 runs git log --format= --name-only starting..baseline without --full-history. scripts/validate_correctness_audit.py:513-520 reuses that helper. scripts/validate_correctness_audit.py:501-505 rejects merges only in baseline..HEAD. The exact-candidate probe at /home/smithers/projects/nemesis-audit-r01/probes/candidate2-prov-results.json (SHA-256 432db00792cba00c3e6c965c8c12a7e4725e0aafacb3a59fa6a7a7133c3f667a) records baselineIsMerge=true, historicalLaneFilesResult=[], simplifiedLogContainsLeak=false, and fullHistoryLogContainsLeak=true for docs/qa/implementation-readiness/correctness-audit/packets/leaked.json.
findings.reproduction: Run the saved bounded probe with the exact candidate scripts. It creates a temporary Git repository, commits packets/leaked.json on a side branch, deletes it on that branch, and merges the restored branch as the baseline. The candidate helper returns []; the same range with git log --full-history contains the leaked path. This reproduces the candidate-1 PROV-001 path-simplification mechanism at the still-unfixed starting-HEAD-to-baseline boundary.
findings.recommendation: Make historical_lane_files traverse full history, add a merged-side-branch introduce/delete negative control, and enforce a linear prebaseline ancestry contract by rejecting merge commits in lockedStartingHead..baseline (including a merge baseline) unless a separately specified and reviewed topology is intended. Apply the same full-history rule to every path-history query rather than only post-seal immutable-path checks.

findings.title: Dependency-level artifacts are not required to share one wave seal commit
findings.claim: The validator enforces an immediate direct child only per artifact and per unit. It does not require all packet, completeness, blind, comparison, or adjudication artifacts at one dependency level to share the common pre-seal HEAD and single wave commit required by the methodology. A diagonal pipeline can interleave packet B with completeness A, completeness B with blind A, and blind B with comparison A while every artifact seal and per-unit dependency check passes. That topology places a blind artifact and another unit's post-reveal comparison in the same commit, so Git provenance cannot prove the blind bytes were finalized before the comparison was available.
findings.evidence: docs/qa/implementation-readiness/correctness-audit/methodology.md:42 requires one common pre-seal HEAD and one direct-child wave seal commit for all artifacts at a dependency level. scripts/validate_correctness_audit.py:319-387 validates each artifact independently; lines 419-430 compare only a record with its own preceding-lane commit; lines 731-737 require packet pre-seals merely to be at or after the lock; lines 1766-1768 collect only comparison commits and do not collect or cardinality-check every lane's wave commit. The exact-candidate diagonalLanePipeline probe records two distinct commits in each packet/completeness/blind/comparison lane while sealFailures=[] and dependencyFailures=[].
findings.reproduction: Run /home/smithers/projects/nemesis-audit-r01/probes/final_specialty_01_probe.py against the exact candidate. Its two-unit temporary history is: packet A; packet B + completeness A; completeness B + blind A; blind B + comparison A; comparison B. validate_artifact_seal, require_lane_preseal, and packet minimum-ancestry checks accept every record. Results are retained in candidate2-prov-results.json with SHA-256 432db00792cba00c3e6c965c8c12a7e4725e0aafacb3a59fa6a7a7133c3f667a.
findings.recommendation: Collect the derived seal commit for every referenced packet, canonical completeness prompt/review, blind prompt/response/derivation, comparison prompt/response/comparison, and adjudication/verification artifact. Require exactly one derived commit and one common declared pre-seal HEAD per dependency wave, require the next wave's common pre-seal to equal the prior wave commit, and add a negative diagonal-pipeline control in addition to the existing positive shared-wave test.

residualRisks: The exact candidate is intentionally prelock: no v2 audit-lock or 140-unit post-lock lane graph exists, so the complete public post-lock validator path could not be exercised on real lane artifacts without creating prohibited repository state.

The progress-history helper accepts structurally valid future artifact references in isolation, but no end-to-end exact-hash bypass was established against the self-referential direct-child seal and current artifact-hash checks; this remains test-coverage risk rather than an accepted finding.

Post-baseline merge rejection, post-seal full-history immutable-byte checks, direct-child derivation, and all-comparisons-before-adjudication checks held in executed controls; the findings are confined to prebaseline history closure and missing global wave cardinality/order enforcement.
